units.translation: 20 Etymologicum Genuinum (AB) Ταίναρος: III 1240–1242. Ἴσθμιον(!) a place in Corinth, but an isthmus is a narrow sea (rather see scholion on I 936/49 g). Ταίναρον is 〈..., Λέρνη added by W〉 a spring in Argos; and of Hyantius the Boeotian grove(!) from Hyas having founded it (Miller, -ήσαντος in AB). Ὀγχηστὸς is (δὲ in B, omitted in A) a city of (τῆς in A, omitted in B) Boeotia.
21 ἱερὰ in P : ἱερὴ in L
22 ὀργιοφάντης in L : ἀργιοφάντης in V (ἀργειο- in A) : ἀργεϊφόντης in P

1242–43a. Of Hyantian Onchestus: of Boeotian; for the Hyantes formerly inhabited Boeotia. Onchestus is a city of Boeotia sacred to Poseidon. Homer (Iliad 2.506): 'and sacred Onchestus, the splendid grove of Poseidon.'
2 scholion on Pindar Isthmian 1.44b, Olympian 3.31a.b; Eustathius on Dionysius Periegetes 803 (357, 41 M.), cf. W 63; 5 scholion on Pindar Olympian 6.148b. 153c; Tzetzes on Lycophron 159, 34 Sch.
1 Βοιωτικοῦ in Et. : εὐβοϊκοῦ in L : (τὸν) Βοιώτιον in P from scholion b
4 ἄλσος with Homer in F

b. Hyantian instead of Boeotian; for the Hyantes are a barbarian people of Boeotia, whence also the proverb 'Boeotian pig.' And Calaureia is also sacred to Poseidon, as Philostephanus says (fr. 18 M. III 31); but formerly it belonged to Apollo, and Pytho to Poseidon, and they exchanged [that is, they swapped].
8 scholion on Aeschylus Eumenides 27; scholion on Lycophron 617; Strabo VIII 373 sq.; Pausanias II 33, 2. X 5, 6; Eustathius on Dionysius Periegetes 498
9 deleted by W 54
c. Calaureia: an island near Troezen. LmP

1244a. And the Haemonian rock: the Thessalian Petra. It is a place in which a contest of Poseidon is held, so that from the place he is called Petraeus. Pindar (Pythian 4.246): 'son of Poseidon Petraeus.'
12 scholion on Pindar Pythian 4.246b
13 Πίνδαρος — Πετραίου in P : omitted in L
b. Geraestus: a cape of Euboea. LgP
1251. ἀαγέες: unbroken, inflexible.
1254. 〈ῥαιστήρ:〉 hammer. Sm
1258. 〈ἐπερρώσαντο〉 περὶ σθένεϊ σφριγόωσαι: they were at their peak, more vigorous in strength, they moved with taut energy, stretched and bursting with power; for σφριγανόν is the strong and solid.
1260. σκαρθμῷ: with the foot. LgSm(P)
1262. ἐπαγαίετο: he rejoiced, he exulted. LgGgSmP
22 ἐγαυρία in LP : omitted in GS
1266a. 〈μεταπαιφάσσουσαν:〉 shining. Lm
b. μεταπαιφάσσεσθαι is also written μεταπαιφάσσουσαν. In either form it means to shine through. P
1268–69a. And then they were not going to be far from the contests for a long time. Lm (P)
b. κληῖδες are the benches on which the rowers sit.
1 Apollonius Sophista, Lexicon Homericum 100, 8 B.; Hesychius κληῖδες; scholion on Lycophron 295; 3 Eustathius 1404, 55
1270. Ἀρήιον: the place near the sanctuary of Ares, where also the fleece is.

1271–72. βαλβίς is the line on which the runners step, but it also means the cutting of a well. The sense: it stood as far from the city as the turning post from the starting line, that is, the starting point.
3 -βάλλουσιν in L : -βαίνουσιν in P
5 ἀφεστήκει in K : ἀφέστηκεν
